title.en: The World of Limitless Possibilities: an interview with Dr. Deepa Malik

text.en: What would you do if doctors said you would never walk again? Dr. Deepa Malik chose to turn that moment into a world of limitless possibilities. Her interview shows how courage changes lives.

The interviewer introduces Dr. Deepa Malik, listed by the International Paralympic Committee among the ten most inspirational women para-athletes in the world.
At 29 she was diagnosed with a spinal tumour. After surgery she was paralysed from the waist down and told she would be bound to a wheelchair.
She said she had two choices: waste her life in regret or transform it into a world of limitless possibilities.
Loving sports and having been a swimmer, she switched to para-athletics. Her breakthrough was the silver medal in shot-put at the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games.
She is the first Indian woman para-athlete to win an Asian Games athletics medal and India's first female Paralympic medallist in any sport.
She believes physical limitations do not define potential and supports the idea of ability beyond disability. Her main challenge was society underestimating her abilities, overcome with mental resilience and family support.
She says sports challenge stereotypes because people who see para-athletes' strength and skill drop their preconceived notions.
She works for inclusivity: emotional health of persons with challenges, women's outdoor adventure, equipment for para sportspersons, and awareness sessions in schools. Her advice is that every setback is an opportunity and disability is a unique strength to be unleashed.

problem.en: Separate fact from opinion: 'I secured the silver medal in Rio in 2016' and 'It was a moment of personal victory'.

text.en: The first sentence can be checked in records.
The second is her own feeling.
Facts are provable; opinions express beliefs.

points.en: Dr. Malik turned a tragedy into achievement.
Facts can be proved; opinions are beliefs.
Setbacks are opportunities to prove strength.
